about: Product atlas (worldfill/build_product_atlas.py for part B, worldfill/build_products_c.py for part C): the world product list and, per area of the ways-of-life survey, the year each product is first made there, first brought there, and gone. Part B's 132 rows are hand-written estimates (estimate=true) from the history of each product. Part C's rows are derived (derived=true) and carry a `source` naming the register each year came from: the technology atlas, the mineral register, or a parent product.

products.name: Wheat and barley
products.note: Mehrgarh about 7000 BCE; the Americas only after 1492

products.name: Rice
products.note: African rice in the Niger delta about 1500 BCE

products.name: Maize
products.note: the Columbian exchange: the Old World only after 1492

products.name: Potatoes
products.note: the Andes; Spain about 1570; India with the Portuguese, early 1600s (common much later)

products.name: Taro, yams and breadfruit
products.note: taro at Kuk in New Guinea about 7000 BCE; the Lapita people in the Pacific

products.name: Bread from bakeries
products.note: villages bake flatbread at home; bakeries are in towns (the good BREAD)

products.name: Crystal sugar
products.note: India under the Guptas; a luxury in Europe until the 1700s; beet sugar in Europe from about 1810

products.name: Sugar cane
products.note: domesticated in New Guinea; to India and China by 500 BCE; the Arabs carried it round the Mediterranean; Columbus took it to Hispaniola in 1493

products.name: Beer and grain wine
products.note: Sumer; rice wine in China; sorghum beer in Africa; chicha in the Andes

products.name: Tea
products.note: China; Europe from 1610; Assam from about 1840 (a daily drink in India only in the 1900s); Georgia 1890s

products.name: Coffee
products.note: Yemen in the 1400s; Baba Budan's seeds in Mysore about 1670

products.name: Cacao and chocolate

products.name: Chillies
products.note: with the Portuguese to Goa in the 1500s

products.name: Spices (pepper, cinnamon, cloves)

products.note: cuneiform, about 3200 BCE to about 75 CE

products.name: Palm-leaf books
products.note: South India; paper took over

products.name: Paper
products.note: China about 105; Samarkand 751; Baghdad 794; Spain 1150; the Delhi sultans; in Mexico brought by the Spanish from 1521 and made at Culhuacan from about 1580 (bark paper before that is its own row)

products.name: Bark paper (amate)
products.note: the oldest known piece 75 CE (Huitzilapa, Jalisco); Maya huun from the 5th century; Maya and Aztec books; mostly banned after the Spanish conquest and replaced by European paper

products.name: Bamboo and wooden slips
products.note: precursors from the late Shang (about 1250 BCE); the earliest surviving slips 5th century BCE; the standard writing material of the Han; largely given up for paper by the 4th century CE

products.name: Wax tablets
products.note: a writing board in the Uluburun wreck (14th century BCE); Greeks from the mid-8th century BCE; Roman and medieval notes and accounts (Enns hospital records from 1500); paper notebooks took over in the 1500s, though a few markets kept them longer; Egypt with Greek schools (estimate)

products.name: Printed books

products.name: Newspapers

products.name: Apples and pears
products.note: from the wild apple forests of the Tian Shan; spread west along the Silk Road, and named varieties only after grafting was learned
products.source: Khoury et al. 2016 for the region of diversity; the archaeological literature for the date; the technology atlas for when farming arrives

products.name: Citrus fruit (oranges, lemons, limes)
products.note: oranges and mandarins from the east; the citron reached the West first, by way of Persia, and the sour kinds came to the Mediterranean in Roman times
products.source: Khoury et al. 2016 for the region of diversity; the archaeological literature for the date; the technology atlas for when farming arrives

products.name: Dates (khajoor)
products.note: among the first fruit trees domesticated, in the Levant and the river valleys of the south
products.source: Khoury et al. 2016 for the region of diversity; the archaeological literature for the date; the technology atlas for when farming arrives

products.name: Olives
products.note: domesticated in the Levant with the vine and the fig; the oil is older than the fruit as a food
products.source: Khoury et al. 2016 for the region of diversity; the archaeological literature for the date; the technology atlas for when farming arrives

products.name: Peas

products.source: Khoury et al. 2016 for the region of diversity; the archaeological literature for the date; the technology atlas for when farming arrives

products.name: Soybeans

products.name: Sweet potatoes

products.name: Tomatoes
